about: tools/workflows/recipes: telling the person one thing is one row of the notices table every notice workflow renders (devices, notices, with kind and key). Replaces tool:tell-the-person, retired with tools/tell-the-person; a step that tells the person something runs this.

payload.label: Tell the person
payload.job: Tell the person one thing: keep one notice (a title, a body, a kind and, when there is one, a link) in the notices of the person's own database, the table their devices read and the read, mark-read and act workflows use. A notice with a key is kept once, however often it is told.
payload.produces: One row of the person's notices, told:<id>, or the one already kept under the same key.

source.from: tool:tell-the-person (retired in 05f587fee) and the notices table of workflow:read-my-device-notices, read on trillion-workshop origin/main
source.note: Telling is one insert into the store's own notices table; delivery to a device is the device's route, read by workflow:read-my-device-notices. Any step that tells the person something runs this workflow with its own words.

database.description: The name of the person's own database, the one the notices live in (the store the account keeps its rows in).

title.description: What the person reads first, in a few plain words

body.description: The rest of what they need to know or do, in plain words

kind.description: What sort of notice it is, in the person's own words for it (needs-you when none)

key.description: A name for this one thing; told again under the same key it is not kept twice

url.description: Where the person goes to act on it

steps.title: Make the notice tables if they are absent, with kind and key
steps.do: Run the statements of this step's sql, in order, through tool:run-sql-in-my-database with database = input.database. They only create what is missing, so a run where both tables exist changes nothing. Submit {rendered: true}.

sql.name: devices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (id text PRIMARY KEY, platform text NOT NULL CHECK (platform IN ('live', 'web-push', 'apns')), token text, app_build text, registered_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), last_seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())

sql.name: notices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notices (id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, device_id text REFERENCES devices (id), title text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', body text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', url text, made_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), read_at timestamptz, acted_at timestamptz)

sql.name: kind-and-key
sql.text: ALTER TABLE notices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS kind text, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS key text

steps.title: Keep the notice once
steps.do: Run the statement named tell of this step's sql through tool:run-sql-in-my-database with database = input.database and params [title, body (empty when none), kind (needs-you when none), key (null when none), url (null when none)]. When it returns a row, that is the notice: answer {id: "told:<id>", kept: true, said: "Told the person: <title>."}. When it returns none, a notice under that key was already kept: run the statement named kept with params [key] and answer {id: "told:<id>", kept: false, said: "Already told under <key>."}. Nothing else is written.

sql.name: tell
sql.text: INSERT INTO notices (title, body, kind, key, url) SELECT $1::text, coalesce($2::text, ''), coalesce($3::text, 'needs-you'), $4::text, $5::text WHERE $4::text IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM notices WHERE key = $4::text) RETURNING id

sql.name: kept
sql.text: SELECT id FROM notices WHERE key = $1::text ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
